HEADLINE: Suspect in deadly Paris suburb shooting sent for psychiatric observation

THE DEVELOPMENT
- The man suspected of Friday's gun attack near Paris "has left custody and been placed under psychiatric observation, French anti-terrorism officials have said."
- The National Anti-Terrorist Prosecutor's Office (PNAT) said he will be observed to evaluate whether his "psychiatric health is compatible with pursuing his interrogation".
- PNAT said the move followed guidance from a psychiatric expert, and that the evaluation will determine whether the suspect should remain in police custody and is "likely to last 48 hours".
- PNAT said the suspect was also found to have cannabis and cocaine in his bloodstream.

THE SUSPECT
- Named in French media as 39-year-old Kevin T. The BBC does not print a surname. DO NOT INVENT ONE.
- Known to police before the attack but not to France's intelligence services, per local media.
- PNAT previously said he had four previous convictions that had been "automatically expunged".
- Thought to have used an old semi-automatic weapon, firing in bursts from his car window.
- Le Monde and AFP report that a Bible, a Quran and a copy of Adolf Hitler's Mein Kampf were found at his home, citing a source close to the investigation. Le Monde and AFP are BOTH APPROVED. This is usable, attributed, and it is the detail that cuts against a purely psychiatric framing.

THE ATTACK AND THE CASUALTIES
- One person killed and five others injured on Friday when the attacker opened fire from his car, first in Trappes and then in nearby La Verriere, "appearing to target people of migrant origin".
- The person killed: Pengo Bossio Wangi, a 26-year-old French-Congolese martial artist, named as the fatality on Saturday. His mixed martial arts club's tribute: "On the mats as off them, he was one of those who lead by example: present, respectful, always ready to lift others up. His smile, his energy and his generosity will remain etched in our walls and in our hearts."
- Three of the injured were taken to hospital in a serious condition, including a 12-year-old girl who remains in a critical condition.
- Nicolas Dainville, mayor of La Verriere, told France Info on Sunday that he had spoken to the girl's mother by phone and confirmed she was "doing better". Another injured resident was recovering; a third remained in a critical condition. FRANCE INFO IS NOT IN SOURCES.md — cite the BBC reporting the mayor.

THE CONTESTED FRAMING — THIS IS WHY THE STORY IS WORTH A LINE
- Emmanuel Macron, President of France, called it a "racist terrorist attack", adding that people had been targeted over their skin colour or religion, and that it marked a "turning point in the life of our Republic and our nation".
- The lawyer for Pengo Bossio Wangi told French media the move to place the suspect under observation was "very rare", and ALLEGED that it was being used to portray the suspect as criminally irresponsible rather than as having acted deliberately. The lawyer is NOT NAMED by the BBC. Do not name him.
- So the tension is explicit: the head of state has called it racist terrorism, the anti-terror prosecutors have moved the suspect to psychiatric evaluation, and the victim's lawyer says that move is being used to blunt the deliberateness of the act.

SECOND APPROVED SOURCE FOR THE CENTRAL CLAIM: NOT ESTABLISHED. CNN's world index carried "Macron says Paris suburb shooting that killed one person was terrorist and racist act" — that is Friday/Saturday's story, not the psychiatric-observation development. THE PSYCHIATRIC OBSERVATION IS BBC-ONLY among the sources I reached, though the BBC attributes it to PNAT, a named official body. If you run it, attribute to PNAT via the BBC.
